vocab.definition: a Group 0 element with a full outer shell.

misconceptions.wrong: Noble gases are reactive like other groups.

misconceptions.right: Helium has 2 — but its shell is still full.

misconceptions.wrong: Boiling points fall down the group.

infoPanels.title: FULL OUTER SHELLS
infoPanels.secondaryContent: A full outer shell means no need to gain, lose or share electrons — so they are unreactive.

questions.text: Explain, in terms of electrons, why noble gases are unreactive. [2 marks]
State the physical state of the noble gases at room temperature. [1 mark]
Describe and explain the trend in boiling point down Group 0. [2 marks]
Argon boils at −186°C, krypton at −153°C. Predict a boiling point for neon. [1 mark]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Noble gases have a ______ outer shell, which makes them ______.

questions.text: Suggest why helium is used in balloons and argon in light bulbs. [2 marks]

footer.tip: A full outer shell = stable and unreactive.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does boiling point increase as the atoms get larger?
